refuted.fact: not_said item: "官方從未列出支援語言，也沒有分語言的評測數字，繁體中文表現無任何官方資料。"
refuted.why: The system card's own footnote 1 does point at an official supported-languages list: 'A list of the languages that ChatGPT currently supports can be found here.' linking to https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8357869-how-to-change-your-language-setting-in-chatgpt . I fetched that link: 403. So the list is unreadable from here, but 'never listed' is wrong and a writing agent repeating it would misstate the source. Correct wording: the card links to an official language list that is unreachable from this container, and the card itself contains no per-language evaluation numbers.

refuted.fact: unverified_or_excluded item: "官方 feed 中 2026-06-09 沒有對應項目（6 月只有 6/4 'Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT' 與 6/18 'Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT'）"
refuted.why: The June 2026 feed carries roughly 55 items, and 2026-06-09 itself has three: 'How engineers at Nextdoor use Codex to build without limits', 'What Codex unlocks for Notion', 'Industrial policy for the Intelligence Age'. The conclusion survives - no June item announces a personalization rollout - but the stated reason is false and must not be reused as the justification.

unsupported.fact: sources[1] = https://openai.com/news/rss.xml, and with it verified_fact #1, the only product-side statement in the entire pack ('GPT-5.5 Instant updates ChatGPT's default model with smarter, more accurate answers, reduced hallucinations, and improved personalization controls.')
unsupported.why: BRIEF.md is explicit: 'feed 給的是日期與標題，不是內容 ... sources 放的是文章頁的網址，不是 feed 的網址.' The content itself is real - I matched the description byte for byte including the U+2019 apostrophe - and the feed is genuinely first-party OpenAI, so this is not fabrication or a second-hand source. But as written the pack breaks an explicit BRIEF rule, and the article page that would satisfy it is 403. This also carries the article's whole '預設模型' framing: the word 'default' appears 0 times in the system card (I grepped), so it exists only in the feed line. Editor must decide consciously: grant a documented exception, or drop the feed and lose the 'default model' wording.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts #12, #25 and #26 attach PNG asset paths as their traceability url (.../assets/images/factuality.png, capture_the_flag.png, cve_bench.png) instead of a URL in sources
unsupported.why: Those URLs are not in the sources list, so as recorded the facts are not traceable to a listed source the way the BRIEF requires. The numbers themselves are sound - I opened all three images and read every label myself (Figure 2: 25.3/17.9, 7.4/4.4, 61.3/46.1, 25.2/15.8, 36.4/19.9, 10.1/4.8; Figure 7 pass@12: 88.23/96.3/94.11; Figure 8 pass@1: 86.27/93.1/90.2) and they are the system card's own embedded figures. The fix is mechanical: set url to https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5-instant/introduction . Worth knowing: these percentages are images in the PDF too, so they are absent from the PDF text layer - they cannot be re-verified without viewing the figure.

additional_findings: VERDICT CONTEXT: I tried hard to break this pack and could not break the facts. All 40 verified_facts re-fetched and checked cell by cell; every number, unit, date and verbatim quote matched, including the deliberately preserved OpenAI typo 'CA/DNS Hijakcing' in fact #23. No fact is sourced to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet. No announcement/publication/effective/availability date is conflated. Vendor claims are correctly flagged is_vendor_claim. No guessed URL, model id, document number or identifier - the two things that could only have been guessed (a gpt-5.5-instant API model page, a cdn.openai.com PDF) were probed, came back 404, and were written into unverified_or_excluded rather than used. The remaining problems are sourcing structure and omissions, not fabrication.

MISSING, material: the base-model caveat. Section 3.1 states 'Our evals are run on the base model, without system-level safeguards, to ensure the model's underlying behavior meets our safety bar.' Every Table 1 number the pack plans to print - including the headline regressions gore 0.867→0.703 and sexual 0.857→0.806 - is a bare-model score, not what a user meets in ChatGPT. Without this sentence the article overstates the regressions in exactly the direction the editorial brief says to avoid.

MISSING, material: the baseline-drift caveat. Section 2 states 'Note that comparison values from previously-launched models are from the latest versions of those models, so may vary slightly from values published at launch for those models', and section 3.1 repeats it. This means every GPT-5.3 Instant figure the article prints (0.867, 0.995, 25.3%, 49.6 ...) is a re-measured value, not the number published in the GPT-5.3 Instant system card. Any before/after sentence needs this framing.

MISSING, material: a second production-prevalence disclaimer. The researcher captured only the hallucination-section one (fact #11). Section 3.1 carries its own: 'These evaluations were deliberately created to be difficult. They were built around cases in which our existing models were not yet giving ideal responses ... Error rates are not representative of average production traffic.' The brief's proposed table comes from section 6 and the safety regressions from section 3.1, so both disclaimers are needed.

MISSING, material: the category rename. Section 3.1 note: 'to deduplicate overlaps between our previous "hate" and "harassment" categories, we are merging "harassment" and "hate" into a single evaluation. Additionally, we have renamed our previous "violence" category to "gore" in order to more clearly distinguish it from requests related to illicit violent behavior; this is a naming change, not a change in the underlying evaluation.' A footnote defines gore as 'graphic or gratuitously gory content ... does not include violent roleplay, violent ideation, or facilitation of violent activity'. The pack's headline regression is the gore row, so the article must carry OpenAI's own definition or Chinese readers will read 血腥 as 暴力.

MISSING: the biological capability results, which cut against a 'more capable' framing and belong in a balanced piece. Multimodal troubleshooting virology, 350 held-out SecureBio questions: 'All models exceed the median domain expert baseline of 22.1%.' ProtocolQA Open-Ended, 108 questions rewritten as open-ended, 19 PhD baseliners: 'All models underperform the consensus expert baseline (54%).' Tacit knowledge: 'GPT-5.5 Instant just outperforms the consensus expert baseline of 80% when including refusals and safe completions, and underperforms 80% when excluding them.' TroubleshootingBench, 52 protocols and 12 PhD experts: 'GPT-5.5 Instant performs below the comparison models, and below the expert baseline of 36.4%.'

MISSING: one of the very few consumer-facing statements readable outside the 403 wall. Section 3.3 closes: 'We've strengthened ChatGPT's ability to recognize subtle warning signs across long, high-stakes conversations and trained the model to respond safely in acute situations, including self-harm.'

BETTER SECOND SOURCE the researcher missed, for the '後來被取代' line: the API changelog has an Aug 6, 2026 entry reading 'Updated the chat-latest snapshot, which points to the latest model available in ChatGPT for Plus and Pro users. We recommend leveraging GPT-5.6 Sol for production API usage.' The chat-latest description stops saying 'latest Instant model' on that exact date - first-party corroboration of the handover from the API side, independent of the August system card, and it is already in sources.

chat-latest lineage, fully confirmed by me and useful for the 'moving pointer' point the pack rightly insists on: Feb 24 released gpt-5.3-chat-latest; Mar 16 updated it; May 5 released chat-latest; May 28 released again; Jun 24 updated; Aug 6 repointed to the Plus/Pro model. Fact #34's 'June 24' is correct. Note the May 28 entry reads 'the latest improvements' where the May 5 entry reads 'our latest improvements' - the researcher's '幾乎相同' is accurate, not sloppy.

Figure 1 (jailbreaks) inspected: a line chart with a labelled 0-100% y-axis and error bars but no per-point value labels. GPT-5.5-Instant (red) sits below GPT-5.3-Instant (green) at every attacker budget, and above GPT-5.1-Instant and GPT-5.2-Instant at most budgets. The refusal to read numbers off it is the right call. The 'above 5.1 and 5.2' detail is available if the writer wants the regression framed against the whole Instant line rather than one predecessor.

PDF cross-check done independently: root /Count = 21 confirms 21 pages; cover text is 'GPT-5.5 Instant System Card OpenAI May 4, 2026'. Table values 0.703, 0.806, 0.963, 0.481, 0.0101, 51.4, 38.4, 92.3, 76.9, 1.47, 2.99, 3.92 are all present in the PDF text layer; the Figure 2/7/8 percentages are not, because those are images in the PDF as well. So 'PDF 表格數字與 HTML 版逐格核對一致' holds for tables and cannot hold for figures.

Date handling is clean and I found no conflation. Feed pubDate Tue, 05 May 2026 10:00:00 GMT; hub page 'Published May 5, 2026'; hub home 'May 05, 2026'; changelog 'May 5' entry - four official channels agree. The PDF cover's May 4 and the sitemap lastmods (announcement 2026-09-15T11:52:22.071Z in both /product/ and /release/; system card 2026-05-22T19:27:50.474Z in both /safety/ and /publication/ - all four re-confirmed by me) are correctly kept separate from the event date. 68 hreflang alternates on the announcement URL, confirmed, including zh-Hant, ja-JP, ko-KR.

Arithmetic check on the excluded '52.5%' claim: (10.1-4.8)/10.1 = 52.48%. The researcher was right to refuse to attribute it to OpenAI - that sentence appears nowhere on any reachable first-party page, and the instruction to write '10.1% 降到 4.8%' instead is correct.

Confirmed the researcher's candidate-list correction: docs/news-2026-batch-4/candidates-tech-and-ai.md line 132 does read '| 2026-05-05 | GPT-5.5 Instant: smarter, clearer, and more personalized | 站上只有 4/23 的 GPT-5.5，這是不同型號 |', and the system card does say 'there is not a model named GPT-5.4 Instant' and 'we refer to GPT-5.5 as GPT-5.5 Thinking to avoid confusion with the instant model'. The same-day 'New ways to buy ChatGPT ads' item (Tue, 05 May 2026 00:00:00 GMT) exists as described; I also found a third 10:00 GMT item that day, 'Unlocking large scale AI training networks with MRC', category Engineering - not this topic.

Minor, not an article fact: sourcing_notes records 1,194 feed items and a newest pubDate of 2026-09-16 13:00 GMT; I see 1,195 items and 2026-09-16 16:00 GMT. The feed moved during the checking day. It demonstrates the BRIEF's own 'live document' warning and does not affect any recorded fact.
